recommended_next_phase: Phase 149O.20L.1 -- Readiness Contract/Schema Evolution: amend HMRC-001 to add a new HMRC-REQ-054 bullet requiring full HBDC Class-B deployment conformance, and define the mapping-function contract text (mirroring certification_status_satisfies_readiness's closed-enum precedent). No production code change. Followed by 149O.20L.2 (independent contract verification), 149O.20L.3 (production readiness integration), and 149O.20L.4 (independent production integration verification); only after 149O.20L.4 may CBV-S10 close.
summary: Phase 149O.20L -- Class-B Full-HBDC Readiness Contract / Integration Analysis (**149O.20L): architecture/contract/integration analysis resolving CBV-S10 (READINESS CONTRACT/INTEGRATION GAP) at the analysis level only -- no production code, no HMRC-001/HMIC-001/HBDC-001 contract amendment, no provisioning, no certification, no activation, no Permission Broker work, no runtime change. Reconstructed the current HATP activation-readiness contract and its live production realization from primary source (not from prior-phase summaries): the sole production entrypoint assess_hatp_mandatory_activation_readiness (hatp_mandatory_cutover.py) is governed by HMRC-REQ-054's six-bullet conjunction (docs/contracts/HATP_MANDATORY_ROLLBACK_CONSUMPTION_CONTRACT.md); live production evaluates seven checks, not six -- the seventh, repository_deployment_identity_valid, is a pre-existing identity prerequisite the implementation already owns but HMRC-REQ-054's text does not itself enumerate. Proved, not assumed, that no existing readiness term already requires full HBDC Class-B deployment conformance: class_b_protected_storage_available's entire computation is `protected_root.is_dir() and not protected_root.is_symlink()` -- a two-predicate directory-existence-and-non-symlink check, a strict subset of the roughly two dozen HBDC-REQ items verify_class_b_deployment_conformance() aggregates across topology/environment-lock/Model-A/deployment-identity families. Read HBDC-001 directly: HBDC-REQ-049, HBDC-REQ-055, and CBD-8 already explicitly disclaim mechanical readiness gating as of the contract's current disposition -- the current gap is not an HBDC-001 defect. Built a concrete bypass counterexample in a new, independent test module (18 passed, 0 failed): using an isolated tmp_path fixture and the existing internal test seam (_assess_hatp_mandatory_activation_readiness_at_root, the same seam the 149O.19.5F suite already legitimately uses), all seven live readiness terms were forced satisfied=True (ready is True, reasons == ()); the real, completely un-mocked verify_class_b_deployment_conformance() -- called with no arguments, so it inspects the real host's own interpreter/ACL/venv state, entirely independent of the fixture -- was then freshly, independently invoked in the same test and found not COMPLIANT. This demonstrates threats T1/T2 (HMIC valid, Class-B NON_COMPLIANT or INDETERMINATE, readiness nonetheless positive) as currently true, not merely theoretical. Evaluated refining an existing term (class_b_protected_storage_available) against all six governing disqualifying criteria (semantic-domain mismatch, authority-concept collapse, diagnostic-granularity loss, historical-record misrepresentation, contract-amendment-required-anyway, no other term being a plausible candidate) and rejected the refinement path on every criterion; evaluated whether current production already semantically requires full HBDC conformance and rejected that outcome (contradicted directly by HBDC-001's own disclaiming text and by the concrete counterexample); evaluated whether a deeper architecture conflict exists (circularity, unsafe stale-state authority) and rejected that outcome too -- no import cycle exists (independently reconfirmed by a fresh AST sweep in the new test module and consistent with HMIC-001 section 53.7's own finding), no caching exists (HMRC-REQ-052/HMIC-REQ-113's no-cache discipline), and the existing dual-evaluation architecture (an advisory assess_hatp_mandatory_activation_readiness call, plus a second, lock-held re-check already performed inside _write_cutover_transition's readiness_check callback before every real Cutover Record write) already generically solves freshness/TOCTOU for every current readiness term and would extend to a future Class-B term without new machinery. Selected architecture: full HBDC Class-B deployment conformance must become a mandatory, fail-closed, eighth readiness term, mapped via the exact closed-enum precedent certification_status_satisfies_readiness already establishes for the HMIC term (ClassBConformanceStatus.COMPLIANT maps to True; every other member of the six-member closed vocabulary -- NON_COMPLIANT, INDETERMINATE, ACCESS_ERROR, MALFORMED_STATE, UNSUPPORTED_DEPLOYMENT_MODEL -- maps to False), added inside the single existing assessment function rather than as a parallel gate. This requires a future HMRC-001 textual amendment (HMRC-001 has no pre-existing placeholder bullet for Class-B deployment conformance, unlike its already-filled HMIC-implementation-verification bullet) but does not require any HMIC-001 or HBDC-001 amendment, and only an additive, non-breaking dataclass change (no persisted readiness artifact schema exists today to migrate). Traced non-bypassability end to end via a fresh AST walk: exactly one readiness entrypoint, one internal implementation, one dataclass-construction site, and one activation writer whose lock-held re-check already calls the same assessment function a second time before any real write. Worked the full T1-T7 threat matrix from the governing analysis; T1/T2 concretely demonstrated positive today, T3/T6 structurally guaranteed by the existing AND-conjunction and single-constructor design, T4/T5/T7 resolved by inheriting the existing dual-evaluation architecture rather than inventing new mechanism. CBV-S1 regression: reconfirmed unchanged and not reopened -- HMIC-001 remains v1.3, production remains 28 authority-bearing files / 5 contract-identity members, and this phase found no evidence contradicting the prior closure. Real-host regression reconfirmed read-only: verify_class_b_deployment_conformance() returned NON_COMPLIANT; assess_hatp_mandatory_activation_readiness(...).ready returned False. CBV-S10: OPEN -- READINESS INTEGRATION ARCHITECTURE DERIVED -- CONTRACT/IMPLEMENTATION WORK PENDING (this analysis-only phase did not close it). Class-B: CONTRACT VERIFIED -- VERIFIER REPAIR LINE INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED -- HMIC SOURCE BINDING INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED -- NOT PROVISIONED (unchanged). HATP production remains NOT READY. Runtime remains Observed / observe / unavailable, unchanged throughout. Recommended next phase: Phase 149O.20L.1 -- Readiness Contract/Schema Evolution (not begun by this phase).
